title: Ellis Burton, the Topeka restaurant, Valetta and the 1929 crash
summary: He recalls Ellis Burton protecting him, opening a Topeka restaurant, writing 'Valetta', the crash and crystal radios.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Now I worked...I was a friend of Ellis Burton.. I had a problem with a woman and Ellis told...so, I'm told he said to a policemen that"It you say anything else to Sammy Price, don't come around me any more."

But anyway, I stayed my time out in Kansas City and I felt like, I guess, a disciple, that I was supposed to stay in a certain place, you know, until my time was out and then move on. In the meanwhile, I opened a restaurant in Topeka, Kansas. I was going with a girl named Valetta. I wrote a song...

You got that record? All right. Well, I wrote a song, "Valetta," and we had this restaurant, and when they had the crash--that was in '29--I had a lot of food on the stove, two or three cars and, you know, all of that, and no customers. And, just like I said, I didn't realize then, even 'til '29-- and I had traveled extensively and had read, of course...You know, in the beginning, and in the early twenties, you know, you didn't have radios like you have. Now you had these radios with earphones, like those earphones, and you had to touch a little--did you ever see that crystal set? And you touched that, and if you put it on the right spot, you could

hear it; but a lot of times--Earl Hines used to come from Chicago, you know, and we didn't have but one, one or two earphones, you know...we'd have one that you listen in and we'd all be trying to listen and sometimes somebody would touch that crystal and it would go off at the point, and you just couldn't hear it. When you'd come back when you'd get it again, he says, "Ladies and Gentlemen, Earl Hines will at 9.30 be on tomorrow night (laughter). But be that as it may, I think that we did pretty good with the conditions as they were.
